problem: Federated VLN (FedVLN) aggregates all clients with FedAvg into one global model, which is suboptimal under extreme non-IID data because each client is a different house with its own layout and instruction style. Generic pFL methods (backbone/head split, full-model adaptation) ignore VLN's tightly coupled encoder-decoder structure, so indiscriminate personalization can hurt grounding.
motivation: VLN data comes from private homes, so training must be federated for privacy. Fig. 1 and Fig. 3 show large cross-client performance variance and heterogeneity in scale, complexity, path and instruction length, so one global model cannot serve every environment. Different VLN modules differ in environment sensitivity, so personalization should be selective and adaptive.
key_idea: Personalize only the VLN layers that matter: always the encoder-decoder projection, plus decoder layers chosen per client and round by learned mixing coefficients. Fuse global and local parameters element-wise on those layers and keep the critic local.
insight: Selective personalization beats both extremes. Personalizing all layers collapses performance (RxR ResNet SR 32.7 vs 39.9 for no personalization), because clients have too little data to learn both general and local knowledge. Personalizing only the chosen layers gives SR 40.1 and SPL 36.7 with lower cost. Gains are largest on trajectory-quality metrics (nDTW, CLS, NE), and convergence is faster.
method: Module split: the encoder embedding and BiLSTM are shared globally; the encoder-to-decoder projection is always personalized; the critic stays local and is never aggregated; decoder layers are chosen adaptively.

Adaptive layer selection: each decoder layer gets a learnable mixing coefficient alpha in [0,1]. The fused parameters are (1-alpha)*global + alpha*previous local. Alpha is learned by minimizing teacher-forcing imitation loss on a small local batch (lr 0.1, 2 steps). Layers with alpha >= delta=0.6 are personalized.

Fine-grained parameter fusion: for personalized layers, the initialization is theta_local + W ⊙ (theta_global - theta_local) with element-wise learnable W in [0,1]. W is trained with the IL loss (lr 0.1, 1 step per round, fully optimized only in round 2). Non-selected layers inherit the global parameters.

Local training and aggregation: each client trains 5 epochs with the standard EnvDrop IL+RL objective, then uploads the encoder and decoder. The server does dataset-size-weighted FedAvg (participation rate 0.2). Only the encoder and decoder are transmitted; the critic is not.

setting.backbone: EnvDrop-style VLN agent: BiLSTM instruction encoder + attention LSTM decoder + critic, trained from scratch with ResNet-152 or CLIP visual features
setting.training_data: R2R and RxR trajectory-instruction pairs, partitioned by house (one client per Matterport3D building); federated training with no extra data
setting.observation: egocentric panoramic visual features (ResNet-152 or CLIP) + instruction text

numbers_note: The paper never names the evaluation split, so val-unseen is an assumption. Reported metrics are per-client averages, compared against FedVLN's global model values. The R2R ResNet and CLIP rows are printed in the table.
results: pFedNavi beats FedVLN on all metrics for both ResNet and CLIP features. For example, R2R ResNet SR is 54.5 vs 50.7 and RxR CLIP SR is 46.1 vs 43.0. It approaches the centralized EnvDrop (R2R CLIP 60.7 vs 61.5 SR) and even exceeds it on some metrics (R2R CLIP SPL 57.4, nDTW 57.1, NE 3.65). Loss reaches 3.0 in 208 rounds vs 288 for FedVLN (1.38x faster), but a round costs 3.6 min vs 2.2 min.
limitations: Per-round wall-clock time is higher than FedVLN (3.6 vs 2.2 min) because of the extra alpha and W optimization steps.
Evaluated only on old LSTM-based agents (EnvDrop-style) on R2R and RxR, with simulated clients on a single machine; no modern transformer or LLM-based VLN agents and no real-world deployment.
The evaluation split is unspecified, and personalized metrics are per-client averages compared against a global model, which may favor pFedNavi.
